basis: No findings filed (items 0-8 are outside-window or searched-and-empty); annual report restates a known balance sheet; casebook no-finding Australian names moved randomly.
against: Placement paper (item 2) and gold beta can move a small explorer several percent either way.

basis: Nothing in window (items 0-9); release likely lands before the window opens; only the placement allotment (item 3) trades in it.
against: Allotment-day selling by underwater placees could push it down several percent.

basis: Matches the casebook's repeatedly-right pattern of an official category series plus a direct peer covering the exact reported window (items 0 and 5: ONS hardware +4.85% in Q2, Wickes step-up), against a stale July consensus (item 2) and a record, still-building short (item 1).
against: The +6.25% five-day run-up already prices part of the relief, the drought hit seasonal categories (item 3), and a plain reiteration has twice been sold on this name.

basis: Unreported activist stake from a sale-pushing fund (item 0) plus a relief case on the Novartis/BMS pause if the guide is held (item 1), with a fast-building aggregate short (item 2).
against: Undisclosed one-off charges in H1 EBITDA (item 3), a top holder still distributing (item 4), and this name has fallen on every observed results day.

basis: The FY organic guide needs an implausible Q4 snap-back (item 0) and the last full results statement fell 9.9% (item 1); matches the casebook pattern of guide-arithmetic misses that were right on several names.
against: A buyback absorbing about 40% of daily volume (item 2) and the undisclosed pension buyout (item 3) give a real bid under the print.

basis: Shareholder-approved 448p cash offer pins the price; interims are irrelevant (first-hunter context, item 0).
against: Only a surprise rival bid or scheme failure could move it, and nothing points to either.

basis: Pinned under a final 250p cash offer the Panel bars from revision (item 0); the stock has held a 1.5p range for 16 sessions.
against: Deal-break news inside the window would move it sharply, but none is scheduled.

basis: Unguided IEEPA refund worth about 9% of market cap that peers booked in the same window (item 0), with a -13% 20-day run-up into the print.
against: In the casebook, tariff-refund upside findings split badly (two large misses against two hits), as the market strips one-offs out, and this name's reactions are huge and two-sided.

basis: A +16.5% five-day run-up on no company news (item 14), a mechanically weak quarter after recovery-inflated Q4 (items 2 and 13), and downside skew paid.
against: Consensus revenue looks structurally stale and the company has beaten it heavily (item 0), and the casebook's no-news run-up shorts were right only about half the time.

basis: Matches the casebook's strongest repeated pattern: a government price series for the exact fiscal quarter (item 0: pipe PPI reversed to +1.9% y/y by July) plus a key supplier's same-window print showing price-led strength (item 1), into a stock at a 52-week low with puts bid.
against: Housing starts fell hard in July (item 2), management guided PVC down year on year, and a distributor's margin can lag price.

basis: Two independent hunts found the core brand's paid-acquisition traffic still falling every month after the guide (items 0 and 14), with Meta ad prices unchanged, into a stock that rallied 36-44% above every analyst target; both prior real earnings reactions were -49% and -30% (item 2).
against: Short interest of 23% of float and rising, with calls bid (item 15), plus a GAAP debt-repurchase gain and possible buyback (item 16), can squeeze an in-line print upward.

basis: Record July heat and AHRI shipments (item 0), construction hiring (item 1) and Watsco industry stabilisation (item 2) after a -13.7% five-day drop.
against: These are broad macro proxies of the kind (weather, macro shocks) that pointed the wrong way repeatedly in the casebook, and SaaS prints trade on guidance and NDR, not weather.

basis: A freak 15.8% gross-margin comp that cannot be lapped (item 0) and vinyl turning to decline in the reported quarter (item 1); matches the casebook pattern of negative comp-arithmetic calls on illiquid small caps that were mostly right, and four of five prior prints fell.
against: A $1.5m tariff refund could land in the quarter (item 2), and a 3% real float makes the reaction erratic.

basis: Findings offset: customer concentration and a large new lease (items 0 and 1) against seasonal Q1 cash collection and a CRL bookings read (items 2 and 3).
against: Most prior prints fell double digits, so a negative lean may be the better bet.

basis: Undisclosed $8m tariff refund claim, about 6% of the market cap (item 0), plus industry wholesale orders +8-11% in the window (item 1), after a -16.6% 20-day slide; similar to the casebook's furniture and footwear refund cases that were right.
against: Refund findings were wrong as often as right in the casebook, retail furniture peers were weak (item 1 counter-evidence), and the comp governance issue (item 2) is a blemish.

basis: A locked-in earnout charge makes GAAP look like a large miss (item 1), and a supply-back markup escalator squeezes margin (item 2).
against: The germanium squeeze (item 0) is the bull story, this name has looked through earnout noise before, and the options imply only a 3.5% event move.

basis: The Q1 margin was propped by a 904bp one-off refund (item 0), the greenshoe stabilisation bid has ended (item 1), and the quarter is pre-announced so only the first guide matters (item 2).
against: Debt paydown halves interest from Q3 (item 3), peer demand is firm, and first post-IPO guides tend to be set beatable.

basis: Same-quarter peers all beat, the closest analogue by a lot (item 1), against a guide set off one weak May reading; plus an unguided refund (item 0) and a 10% short at a 52-week low (item 3); matches the casebook's peer read-through pattern.
against: The stock trades on the month-to-date comp, which laps +11-13% this year (item 2), and the last print fell 11% on guidance despite a beat.

basis: No findings; normalised Q4 brackets consensus (item 4) and peer reads are already on the wire (item 5).
against: Four of five prior prints fell 5-19%, so a large move either way is likely.

basis: No direction is available: the only item is an undated Phase 1 readout whose sign cannot be known (item 0).
against: A pipeline update on the call could move a thin retail-driven tape sharply.

basis: A likely below-prior-year Q1 guide against an inflated comp (item 1); last year's equivalent print fell 25%.
against: A probable Q4 beat of about 10% (item 0), the guide level is inferred rather than documented, and the name cannot be traded at about $100k a day.
